title: O*NET Agentic Coverage Dataset
description: A task-level estimate, for all 18,796 O*NET work tasks (the full O*NET task corpus, economy-wide), of how much of each task a current autonomous AI agent could complete end to end with no human in the loop. Labels were generated with a large language model (Claude Sonnet) against a single neutral instrument, applied in one consistent pass across the full corpus, then validated: three independent human annotators each scored all 200 tasks of an audit sample, giving Spearman rho = 0.884 against the model (99.9% of the 0.885 reliability ceiling set by inter-annotator agreement), with a documented mean calibration bias of -0.147 (model conservative relative to humans in absolute level; ranking is not affected). Built as a companion resource to the ATES (Agentic Task Exposure Score) framework and the O*NET Task-to-Ability Mapping Dataset, it also stands alone for research on AI exposure and human-AI task allocation.
